tasks.title: Derive wall PAINT area (perimeter x height) — the missing painting measurement
tasks.notes: A 2D plan has no wall height so painting gets ZERO auto-sqft today. wall paint SF/room = perimeter x height (perimeter from geometry.rings / meta.perimeter; seeder currently DROPS geometry — preserve it). Emit a 'Wall paint area' line per room.

prep.what: Add a wall/ceiling height field to estimates and wire the takeoff seeder to compute wall paint SF = perimeter × height per room, emitting a 'Wall paint area' measurement line.
prep.understand: 2D floor plans have no Z axis — without a height value, painting quantities are always zero. The room perimeter already exists in `geometry.rings` / `meta.perimeter` from the engine, but the seeder currently discards geometry entirely. You need to preserve that geometry through the import, add a project-level height default (with optional per-room override), and compute SF at seeding time. This feeds directly into the trade routing (t46) that comes later today.
approach: Add nullable `wall_height_ft` column to estimates via a new migration
Update the walk-through UI (WalkThroughs/Show.vue) to show a wall height input (project default + optional per-room override)
In TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php, stop discarding geometry — read `meta.perimeter` per room, multiply by wall_height_ft to get wall paint SF
Emit a 'Wall paint area' (SF) line per room in the seeded estimate; surface live 'Wall area' + 'Wall linear feet' stats in the walk-through Show view

tasks.title: Route takeoff measurements to trades at the seam
tasks.notes: Every measurement collapses into kind=custom $0 today, dropping kind+geometry. Switch on kind: area SF→flooring, derived wall SF→painting, LF→trim, count→doors/tile. Tag each line with a trade via core-vs-subbed helper.

prep.what: Stop collapsing all takeoff measurements into `kind=custom $0` — read the `kind` field on each measurement and route it to the right trade line (flooring, painting, trim, tile/doors).
prep.understand: Every room measurement carries a `kind`: `area` (SF of floor), `line` (LF of walls/trim), `count` (doors/fixtures). The wall-paint lines you build in t45 this morning also arrive here as a derived measurement kind — make sure the seeder can handle both engine-native and derived quantities.
approach: In TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php, read measurement.kind instead of hardcoding 'custom'
Add a switch: `area` → flooring SF line, wall-derived (from t45 output) → painting SF line, `line` → trim/wall-linear LF line, `count` → door/tile EA line
Apply trade tagging via ProjectType::isCoreTrade() / group() on each line so the estimate editor shows correct groupings
Smoke-test by seeding an estimate from a sample takeoff project and verifying lines land in the correct trade groups

tasks.title: Label lane v2: M3 vision for outlined-text firms + callout-vs-room filtering
tasks.notes: Caught live on Harborview demo (2026-06-11): rooms show 'unnamed' because PDFTron outlines ALL text (55 live words, zero room labels). v2 = productize M3 tiles lane as opt-in 'read labels (AI)' action + callout-vs-room noise filtering.

prep.what: Build an opt-in 'read labels (AI)' action using the M3 tiles pipeline for firms where all text is outlined (invisible to the free live-text lane), plus add callout-vs-room filtering to suppress false matches.
prep.understand: The free lane works on PDFTron-extractable text. For firms that outline their text (raster-baked labels), zero words are found — rooms show 'unnamed'. The spike (`run_labels_m3tiles.py`) already proves M3 tiles reads these at ~4.3 min/sheet. Three constraints to hold: (1) It costs money → must be metered via the §7a credits event; (2) MINIMAX_AI key must reach the VPS following the t13 secrets pattern; (3) Callout noise is real — Holabird shows stair arrows, FEC boxes, and paragraph notes all get matched as room names.
approach: Create a new opt-in POST /sheets/{id}/label-ai route, queue it as a background RQ job, emit SSE/webhook progress and completion events
Wire MINIMAX_AI key to VPS /opt/takeoff-engine/.env following the t13 secrets pattern (chmod 600, loud-fail guard in compose)
Productize docs/spike/run_labels_m3tiles.py into engine/labels_m3.py, integrating with the existing label-writing flow
Add callout-vs-room filtering: suppress matches > ~4 words, suppress known noise patterns ('UP', 'DN', 'FEC', 'AHU', stair/elevator symbols, multi-line paragraphs)
resources: service/ routes + RQ worker pattern (§8 route list, existing job queuing)
VPS .env + /opt/takeoff-engine deploy (t13 secrets pattern for reference)

tasks.title: Assemblies-per-room → paint/drywall/flooring quantities + wall heights
tasks.notes: assemblies-lite folded into B1 (engine/assemblies.py scaffolded). Full version = room type → assemblies + formulas + heights (one classification → up to 8 quantities, CSI libraries). The last pillar between us and estimator-grade Excel.

prep.what: Build out the full assembly formula engine: given a room classification, derive all relevant quantities (flooring SF, wall paint SF, ceiling SF, drywall area, trim LF) using CSI-based formulas and integrate into the Excel export.
prep.understand: `engine/assemblies.py` is scaffolded but only produces placeholder data. The full version maps room classification → formula set. The critical missing dimension is HEIGHT — a 2D plan has no Z axis, so you need a classification-to-height default table (residential bedroom = 9ft, commercial corridor = 10ft) with a project-level override. Each room then produces up to 8 derived quantities. These feed into `build_sheet_takeoff` as additional Excel rows, making the workbook estimator-grade — this is the last pillar before that milestone.
approach: Define the assembly formula table as a Python dict: classification → list of (quantity_name, formula_fn, csi_category). Start with the 4 high-value ones: flooring SF, wall paint SF, ceiling SF, trim LF
Add a classification→height_ft default table in engine/assemblies.py; accept a project-level `wall_height_ft` override passed through the service layer
Implement the formula engine: accepts a room dict (area_sf, perimeter_ft, height_ft, classification), returns a quantities dict
Integrate with `build_sheet_takeoff` in engine/excel.py so assembly rows appear as additional priced lines per room in the workbook
Run the gauntlet (currently 85 checks) to confirm no regression
resources: CSI MasterFormat Division 09 (finishes: drywall, flooring, paint, trim)
